messages:
sara: quick q — embedding endpoint behavior when clients send mixed inputs? strings, empty strings, "null" items, arrays of tokens, plus questions about truncation, padding and preserving order in batched requests. trying to lock down wording for the SDK docs.

omar: short answer: we preserve input order in the response (1:1). each input -> one embedding entry. empty string -> we still return a vector (deterministic). explicit JSON nulls in the items array are treated as invalid and return 400 for the whole request.

sasha: to add: truncation is token-based (BPE), not char-based. we truncate per-item before encoding into the model. current default max per-item = 8192 tokens for the emb-v2 family. if an item exceeds that we truncate and set per-item metadata in the response (see example).

lee: batch limits: current service enforces max 2000 items per request and a payload size cap ~25MB. if either limit is exceeded we return 413 Payload Too Large. we also have a request-level tokens cap to protect runtime memory—clients will see 429 if rate-of-tokens too high.

sara: ok on order, good. what about output shape guarantees? some customers assume fixed-length floats and index ordering matches inputs. need exact text for docs.

omar: output: we return an array of embeddings where each embedding is a flat list of floats length = model_dim. e.g. for "emb-v2-small" model_dim = 1024. we guarantee same dimensionality for a given model version. if we rollout a new model with different dim we will add a compatibility header and version note in the response metadata, but client SDKs should prefer model names not assume dims.

sasha: also: for truncated items we include a small metadata object adjacent to each embedding in the response: {"truncated": true|false, "truncated_tokens": N} — proposal to help debugging. thoughts?

lee: fine with that, but keep the top-level response compact. maybe only include metadata when truncated==true to avoid payload bloat.

sara: example payload for docs — please sanity-check.

omar: here's an example request + response sketch we can use in the SDK docs:

```json
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "emb-v2-small",
  "inputs": ["hello world", "", "This is a very long document... (truncated by client)" ]
}

// response (simplified)
{
  "model": "emb-v2-small",
  "data": [
    {"embedding": [0.0012, -0.3302, ...], "index": 0},
    {"embedding": [0.0000, 0.0000, ...], "index": 1},
    {"embedding": [0.1002, 0.0021, ...], "index": 2, "meta": {"truncated": true, "truncated_tokens": 912}}
  ]
}
```

sasha: nit: prefer to guarantee index ordering and avoid relying on the index field. also recommend docs tell users to correlate by array position (data[0] -> inputs[0]) in case someone strips index.

lee: also confirm encoding details: we use UTF-8, so clients should be careful with byte-length vs char-length; tokenization happens after UTF-8 decode. multibyte characters count toward token budget.

sara: what about padding? if clients want fixed-size batches on our inference pool, do we ask them to pad vs we pad on server?

omar: we do automatic dynamic batching and we internally pad to nearest block for the model; clients do not need to pad. we do not expose padded vectors — embeddings are computed on the real (possibly truncated) input and returned unpadded.

sasha: backward compat note: if a future model changes dim, we'll expose a response field "model_dimensions" and include a deprecation header for old model names. ops will send a notice to #announce before any breaking change.

sara: final doc checklist from this thread for the SDK writeup:
- state per-item truncation rule (token-based, default 8192 tokens)
- empty string -> deterministic non-null vector
- explicit JSON null in inputs -> 400 (invalid)
- ordering guarantee: response array order matches input order (recommend to correlate by position)
- batch limits: 2000 items / ~25MB payload / token-rate protections -> 413 or 429 as appropriate
- embedding shape: fixed per-model; include guidance to query model metadata if clients assume dims
- truncated items include inline meta when truncated==true (show example)
- server-side padding for batching; returned vectors are unpadded

lee: I'll add these points to the API spec PR. @sasha can you add the small response schema change for the truncation meta? :eyes:

sasha: yup will open a tiny PR with schema + example responses.

devops-bot: deploy status: embedding-service v2.14 currently on canary. No breaking model-dim changes scheduled in this cycle.

sara: thanks everyone — I'll draft the SDK docs and ping for reviews. anyone object to me adding an explicit example showing a client handling empty-string embeddings?

omar: go ahead. :thumbsup:
